# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 37 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalent)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus (ch 1-31) / P.Mich. 130 (ch 32+), Shepherd of Hermas 37 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_037_page_001.jpg

---

## Mandate 7 — Fear God, Not the Devil

**1** "Fear the Lord," he said, "and keep his commandments. As you keep his commandments you will be strong in every deed you do, and your deeds will be beyond compare. For in fearing him you will do everything well. **2** This is the fear you ought to have, the fear that leads to salvation. But do not fear the devil. **3** For if you fear the Lord, you will have mastery over the devil, since he has no power. And where there is no power, there is nothing to be feared. **4** But where there is glorious power, that power commands fear. For everyone who is truly powerful is feared; but whoever has no power is feared by no one. **5** Fear then the deeds of the devil, for they are evil. But fearing the works of the Lord and keeping his commandments, you will live to God." **6** I said, "Sir, I have been strengthened when I heard all these commandments; for I know I will be saved if I keep them." He replied, "You will be saved — you and all who keep these commandments of the Lord."

---

*LOGOS note: The logic of fear here is subtle: we are told to fear the devil's deeds (v.5) but not the devil himself (v.2). This is a practical formulation — we should be alert to what evil deeds produce, without being paralyzed by the devil's perceived power.*
